## Claims
- [proved] From the accepted integral interval/Pieri presentation, the requested target is established for \(p=c=1\) and \(0\le k\le b:=\min(i,j)\): \(M_{d+k}\) has basis \(P_{x,k-x}\) \((0\le x\le k)\), and all positive-degree multiplication relations in degree \(d+k\) are exactly \(\sum_{x=0}^{k-1}\mathbb Z(C_x+C_{x+1})\), where \(C_x=P_{x,k-x}\).

## Strategy
Put \(d=ij\), \(q=i+1\), \(r=j+1\), and
\[
P_{x,y}=s_{((i+1)^x,i^{j-x},y)}.
\]
Every partition in \((i+1)^{j+1}\) containing \(i^j\), of size \(d+k\), uniquely has \(x\) top rows enlarged and final-row length \(k-x\). Since \(k\le\min(i,j)\),
\[
M_{d+k}=\bigoplus_{x=0}^{k}\mathbb ZP_{x,k-x}.
\]

For \(1\le t\le k\) and \(0\le x\le k-t\), Pieri gives, after restriction to the interval,
\[
h_tP_{x,k-t-x}
 =P_{x,k-x}+P_{x+1,k-x-1}
 =C_x+C_{x+1}.
\]
Indeed, an allowed horizontal \(t\)-strip can enlarge either no top row or exactly one top row: enlarging two top rows repeats column \(i+1\). These are precisely the two displayed interval partitions.

Since \(\Lambda_+\) is generated as an ideal by \(h_1,h_2,\ldots\), every positive-degree relation in degree \(d+k\) is a sum of such \(h_t\)-rows, hence lies in
\[
L_k:=\sum_{x=0}^{k-1}\mathbb Z(C_x+C_{x+1}).
\]
Conversely, the \(t=1\) rows are
\[
h_1P_{x,k-1-x}=C_x+C_{x+1}\qquad(0\le x<k),
\]
so every generator of \(L_k\) is a positive-degree multiplication relation. Therefore the relation lattice equals \(L_k\).

For \(k=0\), \(M_d=\mathbb Zs_{i^j}\) and the relation lattice is \(0\).

## Gaps
The argument uses the accepted integral interval/Schur/Pieri presentation. It makes no assertion for \(k>b\), where the displayed unrestricted indexing \(0\le x\le k\) no longer describes the interval.
